key_insight: Physis-Lang argues that language can be more than a description tool: it can become a self-evolving physical representation for video world models. The core breakthrough is a framework that learns and updates physical knowledge in language form to improve physically consistent video prediction.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between visually plausible video generation and physically correct world modeling. Existing video world models often ignore or poorly represent physical laws, leading to outputs that look realistic but break basic physics.
method: Introduces Physis-Lang, a self-evolving language-based framework for representing physical knowledge in video world models.
Learns physical concepts as language representations rather than relying only on extra visual, latent, numerical, or planning signals.
Updates and refines this physical language over time so the model can better predict how scenes evolve under physical constraints.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a simpler and more flexible path to physically grounded video generation and world modeling. It could reduce reliance on complex auxiliary modalities while improving consistency, interpretability, and transferability of learned physics.

paper_title: Physis-Lang: Self-Evolving Language as a Physical Representation for Video World Model
paper_authors: Liming Lu, Xianzheng Ma, Wenkun He, Guanqi Zhan, Yilin Zhao
